rationale: The assistant correctly read the 'twang' as a snapped tension mechanism, which matches the hidden truth, and did not invent anything the customer had not said. However it escalated after only two turns without asking the full model number, which side had lost tension, or whether a broken spring was visible under the plinth, and it never established whether the unit could be pulled out, so the blanket 'not an owner-safe repair' and 'fit new hinges or struts' is overcautious and under-evidenced (Hotpoint units typically use coil springs/cables rather than gas struts). The outcome is safe and points the homeowner in a workable direction, but a real UK homeowner would have been better served by a couple of simple checks and a note that springs are replaced in pairs and need the full model.
